newsitem.title: CANADA: Bull run in Canada energy stocks seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: Bull run in Canada energy stocks seen continuing.

text.p: Surprising strength in oil and natural gas prices and low Canadian interest rates should extend the bull run of Canadian energy stocks, analysts said. The Toronto Stock Exchange's oil and gas subindex blasted through the 7,000 point mark for the first time last week, a showing that industry experts said was sustainable.
"I think it is -- my one-year outlook still shows a lot of upside for a lot of stocks," Ken Faircloth, analyst with brokerage Goepel Shields & Partners, said on Monday.
"I still think there's further upside in the context of a US$20 (a barrel) oil world."
The oil and gas subindex topped 7,000 last Thursday, a level thought elusive last winter when the oils experienced a correction that wiped out more than 700 points of an earlier gain.
The drop came as West Texas Intermediate crude oil prices fell to almost US$19 a barrel.

"The common view is that the index was way oversold in that period of time and now people are thinking, 'We underestimated earnings in the first quarter, prices are looking fairly rosy on oil and natural gas and this is a sector we can't afford not to be in," FirstEnergy Capital Corp analyst Martin Molyneaux said.
Canada's oils sector climbed 56.45 points on Monday to 7,159.53, another new high. The gains came as the broad TSE 300 index jumped one percent to 6487.60, which was also an intra-day record.
Big gainers in energy on Monday included Imperial Oil Ltd, which jumped 1.25 to 67.15, Norcen Energy Resources Ltd, up 1.50 to 35 and recent star Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd, up 0.95 to 32.45.
NYMEX WTI closed on Friday at US$21.63 a barrel, after mostly climbing through May.
"Oil prices were the main thing to swing the psychology," Faircloth said. "It's a bit of a surprise. The market's probably firmer than expected."
Natural gas prices also remained strong after the winter heating season, even in Canada where they have lagged those in the United States for the past few years.

Expected demand from California and the U.S. Pacific Northwest as well as the need to refill depleted storage facilities were expected to keep gas prices strong through the rest of the year, analysts said.
Oil companies were also reaping market benefits from Canada's low interest rates, which served to boost share prices across all sectors, Fairloth said.
Molyneaux said that despite rising stock prices, investors were still able to reap value out of oils, albeit selectively.
"You can't go and take a shotgun to the whole index and think that you're going to see 8,000," he said.

He said possible negatives on the horizon were third-quarter oil prices, which could be hit after this year's summer driving season demand cools, and widening differentials between light and heavy oil. Heavy oil is a main production target for Canadian firms.
